newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-U.S. payroll data seen rebounding in Oct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-U.S. payroll data seen rebounding in Oct.

text.p: U.S. economists look for a significant rebound in additions to U.S. payrolls in October following September's surprise fall.
Markets are braced for a gain of 212,000 in October following September's loss of 40,000, a Reuter poll showed. However, forecasts ranged wildly, from gains of 145,000 to 350,000.
"To really put more juice into the (Treasury) rally it'll have to be 150,000 or lower," said Elliott Platt, director of economic research at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp.
The employment report, considered of late the world's most watched economic indicator, is set for release at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
The unemployment rate is seen unchanged at 5.2 percent.

The initial inclusion of the October 1 minimum wage hike to $5.15 per hour should boost average hourly earnings by 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points, to an overall gain of 0.4 percent, analysts said. The September rise was 0.5 percent.
The October average workweek is seen holding virtually steady at 34.6 hours, against 34.7 in September.
